children: The US materials science company has operationalised a new optical connectivity facility in Pune and plans a larger capacity addition in 2027, while expanding its consumer electronics and pharmaceutical manufacturing businesses in India

US-based materials science company Corning has operationalised a new optical connectivity manufacturing facility in Pune and is preparing a larger capacity expansion in 2027, as rising investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure drive demand for fibre and connectivity products in India.

The new facility manufactures optical connectivity products for data centres and telecommunications networks, complementing Corning's existing optical fibre manufacturing operations in Pune. The company is also preparing to add a larger adjacent facility, with the additional capacity expected to come online in 2027.

"The demand has been growing substantially over the last two years for the fibre, both because of telecom and because of the AI data centres that are coming up in India, and we believe this will at least continue for the next few years," Sudhir N Pillai, Managing Director and President, India, Middle East and Africa, Corning, said.

The expansion comes as AI data centres require dense optical connectivity infrastructure to enable faster communication between graphics processing units (GPUs). Corning is positioning its optical communications business to address these requirements through higher-density fibre, cables and connectivity systems.
AI Data Centres Drive Connectivity Requirements

Pillai said AI data centres have substantially different connectivity requirements compared with conventional cloud infrastructure. "A typical cloud-based data centre and an AI data centre need 10x more fibre in an AI data centre," he added, explaining that connectivity infrastructure needs to scale alongside computing capacity.

Corning has introduced GlassWorks AI, a portfolio of connectivity solutions designed for AI data centres. The portfolio includes optical fibre with a 40 per cent smaller cross-sectional area, cables that are twice as dense as traditional cables and MMC connector systems that offer 36 times higher density.
The products are designed to accommodate more fibre connectivity within existing data centre infrastructure, helping operators address space constraints while increasing computing capacity.

The company's optical connectivity expansion in India builds on its existing optical fibre manufacturing operations in Pune, established in 2012. The new facility adds connectivity products to the manufacturing capabilities available at the location, strengthening Corning's position across the optical communications value chain.
India Manufacturing Footprint
Corning's India operations span optical communications, consumer electronics, pharmaceutical packaging and technology services.

The company established its optical fibre manufacturing facility in Chakan, Pune, in 2012 with an investment exceeding USD 100 million. The plant supplies optical fibre for telecommunications infrastructure and has supported the expansion of India's connectivity networks. The new optical connectivity facility complements this existing operation.

In consumer electronics, Corning is expanding its presence through Bharat Innovative Glass Technologies (BIG Tech), a joint venture with Optiemus Infracom. The Chennai-area facility, inaugurated in December 2025, is India's first dedicated manufacturing facility for finished cover-glass components for mobile consumer electronics.

The plant has entered trial production and is undergoing customer qualification and validation before commercial production scales up. Once fully operational, it is expected to have an annual capacity of 30 million units.

Corning also manufactures pharmaceutical glass tubing in Telangana through a joint venture with SGD Pharma. The products are used by pharmaceutical manufacturers to make ampoules and vials. The company said the facility had already shipped thousands of tonnes of products to Indian pharmaceutical customers.

Its broader India presence includes its corporate headquarters in Gurugram, optical fibre and connectivity manufacturing in Pune, glass finishing in Chennai, pharmaceutical manufacturing in Gujarat and Telangana, and technology and research operations in Pune and Gurugram.
Pillai said Corning's Global Capability Centre (GCC) had grown fivefold since 2024, with the company developing AI capabilities and talent to support its global operations.
Automotive And Sustainability Opportunities

Beyond optical communications, Corning is looking at opportunities in automotive technology, flexible glass and sustainability. In automotive, the company is working with manufacturers to explore replacing copper with optical fibre for faster communication between vehicle systems.

"If your car is becoming more of a computer, then it needs to have a much faster way of communicating between one system to the other system," Pillai said. He added that Corning was working with automotive companies on in-vehicle optical networking, although it did not yet have a solution.

The company is also developing automotive-grade Gorilla Glass, anti-reflective and anti-glare glass technologies, and cold-forming processes that offer greater design flexibility for vehicle interiors.

On sustainability, Corning is using hyperspectral imaging technology to help identify soil deficiencies, plant diseases and water stress. The technology uses drone-mounted cameras to capture spectral images of agricultural land, which can then be analysed to provide insights into soil and crop conditions.

As the company expands its manufacturing operations and technology capabilities, India is emerging as an important market for Corning's optical communications, consumer electronics and pharmaceutical businesses.
